title: Full-Stack SaaS Developer (Next.js, React & WordPress Integrations)
description:
Southwind Marketing is hiring an experienced full-stack developer to join our team and lead the development of Southwind Guardian, a proprietary, cloud-based platform designed to centralize client services, internal operations, website administration, project management and customer collaboration.



This is an ongoing development position, not a one-time freelance project.



Guardian will be the developer's primary initial responsibility. The selected developer will work directly with Southwind leadership and other team members to plan, design, build, test, deploy, maintain and expand the platform.



Guardian will initially support Southwind Marketing's own operations and clients, including municipal governments, economic development organizations, tourism organizations, chambers of commerce, nonprofits and private businesses.



The platform must support clients with and without websites and must be designed for eventual commercialization as a multi-tenant, white-label software-as-a-service platform.



The objective is to build a reliable, secure and scalable system that Southwind can own, operate and continuously improve.



## 2. Platform Objectives



Southwind Guardian will provide a centralized system for:



1. Client account and workspace management.

2. Staff and contractor collaboration.

3. Project management and service delivery.

4. Tasks, deadlines, milestones and deliverables.

5. Customer support and ticket management.

6. Client communications and discussions.

7. Secure file and document sharing.

8. WordPress and Elementor website management.

9. Website content editing, staging, approvals and publishing.

10. Domain, hosting and SSL administration.

11. Website uptime, maintenance and security monitoring.

12. Notifications and operational alerts.

13. Client onboarding and offboarding.

14. Internal reporting and audit history.

15. Integration with Southwind's existing systems.

16. Future white-label agency subscriptions and SaaS functionality.



Guardian must operate as a unified application rather than a collection of disconnected tools.



## 3. Development Responsibilities



The selected developer will be responsible for:



- Reviewing and refining the technical requirements.

- Recommending the application architecture.

- Designing and developing frontend and backend systems.

- Establishing secure databases and APIs.

- Developing WordPress integrations and custom plugins where necessary.

- Building responsive user interfaces.

- Configuring development, staging and production environments.

- Implementing authentication, permissions and tenant isolation.

- Integrating approved third-party services.

- Writing and maintaining automated tests.

- Troubleshooting and resolving application defects.

- Configuring and maintaining Guardian's hosting infrastructure.

- Implementing backups, monitoring and recovery procedures.

- Maintaining technical documentation.

- Participating in planning and progress meetings.

- Providing regular development demonstrations.

- Supporting the platform after launch.

- Developing future Guardian modules and integrations.

- Assisting with other Southwind development assignments when directed.



The developer must communicate technical limitations, risks, dependencies and recommended solutions before making significant architectural decisions.



## 4. User Roles and Permissions



Guardian must provide secure role-based access controls.



### 4.1 Southwind Super Administrator



Full access to platform administration, including:



- All client accounts and workspaces.

- All projects and websites.

- Staff and contractor management.

- Role and permission management.

- Platform configuration.

- Hosting and integration settings.

- Approval and publishing controls.

- Security and audit records.

- System-wide reporting.



### 4.2 Southwind Staff



Authorized access to assigned clients, projects and operational functions, including:



- Project and task management.

- Customer support.

- Client communications.

- Document management.

- Website content administration.

- Content approvals and publishing where permitted.

- Client reporting.

- Website maintenance records.



### 4.3 Contractors



Contractors must have access only to explicitly assigned projects, tasks, files and discussions.



Contractors must not automatically receive access to entire client accounts, unrelated projects, credentials or internal administrative information.



### 4.4 Client Administrator



Authorized client representatives may:



- Access their organization's workspace.

- View assigned projects and deliverables.

- Review project progress.

- Submit support requests.

- Participate in discussions.

- Review documents.

- Approve website content when authorized.

- Manage permitted client users.



### 4.5 Client User



Limited access to explicitly authorized projects, documents, discussions, support requests and approvals.



### 4.6 Future Roles



The platform architecture must accommodate:



- External agency administrators.

- Board and committee members.

- Department representatives.

- Read-only reviewers.

- Additional custom permission groups.



All authorization must be enforced server-side and at the data-access layer where appropriate.



## 5. Multi-Tenant Architecture



Guardian must support multiple independent organizations within one centrally managed application.



Each organization must have its own logically isolated workspace containing:



- Organization information.

- Users and permissions.

- Projects.

- Tasks.

- Tickets.

- Discussions.

- Files and reports.

- Connected websites.

- Domain and hosting records.

- Approvals.

- Activity history.



Southwind administrators must be able to manage multiple organizations from one administrative account.



The platform must support:



- Multiple projects per client.

- Multiple websites per client.

- Clients without websites.

- Multiple authorized contacts.

- Staff working across multiple clients.

- Contractors assigned to specific work.

- Future agency-level tenants with their own customers.



Database relationships and authorization policies must prevent cross-tenant data access.



The developer must implement automated testing that verifies users cannot access unauthorized client records by manipulating URLs, API requests or identifiers.



## 6. Authentication and Security



Required functionality includes:



- Secure user registration through invitation.

- Login and logout.

- Password recovery.

- Multi-factor authentication for privileged accounts.

- Secure session handling.

- Session expiration.

- User activation and deactivation.

- Immediate access revocation.

- Role assignment.

- Security event logging.

- Protection against unauthorized API access.

- Rate limiting for sensitive endpoints.

- Secure credential and secret management.



Use established, actively maintained authentication technology.



Passwords, tokens and secrets must never be stored in plaintext.



The platform must follow modern application security practices, including relevant OWASP guidance.



## 7. Dashboard System



Guardian must provide role-specific dashboards.



### Southwind Dashboard



The administrative dashboard should display:



- Active clients.

- Active projects.

- Open support tickets.

- Pending approvals.

- Upcoming deadlines.

- Overdue tasks.

- Recent activity.

- Website monitoring alerts.

- Outstanding client requests.

- Items requiring staff attention.



### Client Dashboard



Client users should see:



- Their organization's active projects.

- Project status and milestones.

- Assigned tasks where applicable.

- Pending approvals.

- Shared documents.

- Open support requests.

- Recent updates.

- Connected website information.



### Contractor Dashboard



Contractors should see only:



- Assigned projects.

- Assigned tasks.

- Relevant deadlines.

- Authorized discussions.

- Files required for their work.



Dashboards must use real application data and reflect user permissions.



## 8. Project Management



Guardian must provide native project management functionality.



### Project Features



- Create and edit projects.

- Associate projects with clients.

- Assign project owners.

- Assign staff and contractors.

- Set project status.

- Establish deadlines.

- Create milestones.

- Track deliverables.

- Upload project documents.

- Record project activity.

- Archive completed projects.

- Search and filter projects.



### Task Features



- Create and edit tasks.

- Assign tasks to authorized users.

- Set deadlines.

- Establish priorities.

- Track task status.

- Add descriptions and attachments.

- Create subtasks and checklists.

- Add task comments.

- Track overdue work.

- Filter by assignee, project and status.

- Support recurring tasks.



Project Templates



Guardian must support reusable templates for recurring Southwind services.



Examples include:



- Website development.

- Website maintenance.

- Search engine optimization.

- Social media management.

- Marketing retainers.

- Economic development consulting.

- Tourism marketing.

- Reporting and dashboard development.



Templates should create predefined milestones, tasks and deliverables.



## 9. Customer Support and Ticketing



Guardian must include a centralized support ticket system.



Required functionality:



- Create support requests.

- Assign tickets to staff.

- Associate tickets with clients, projects and websites.

- Set priority levels.

- Track ticket status.

- Add internal notes.

- Add client-visible replies.

- Upload attachments.

- Record ticket history.

- Notify relevant users.

- Close and reopen tickets.

- Search and filter tickets.



Internal notes must remain inaccessible to clients.



The architecture must support future ticket routing, service-level agreements and advanced automation.



## 10. Client Communication and Discussions



Guardian must provide threaded discussions associated with:



- Client workspaces.

- Projects.

- Tasks.

- Support tickets.

- Deliverables.



Required functionality:



- Discussion creation.

- Replies.

- File attachments.

- Activity history.

- Authorized participant access.

- Internal-only discussions.

- Client-visible discussions.

- Notifications.

- Search and filtering.



Guardian will not initially replace Southwind Connect's
 and SMS inbox.



## 11. Document and File Management



Guardian must support secure document storage and controlled sharing.



Features include:



- File uploads and downloads.

- Client-specific document organization.

- Project folders.

- Staff-only files.

- Client-visible files.

- Contractor-restricted files.

- File metadata.

- Upload history.

- Secure download authorization.

- File size and type validation.

- Malware scanning or an equivalent protective mechanism.

- Document retention and deletion controls.



Examples include:



- Project deliverables.

- Website mockups.

- SEO reports.

- Marketing analytics.

- Meeting documents.

- Client-provided materials.

- Approved creative assets.

- Consulting reports.



Credentials and sensitive application secrets must be managed separately from ordinary document storage.



## 12. WordPress and Elementor Integration



WordPress and Elementor integration is a central feature of Guardian.



The platform must securely connect to existing WordPress websites and allow authorized users to manage specifically approved content without unrestricted WordPress administrator access.



### 12.1 Website Connections



Guardian must support:



- Connecting WordPress websites.

- Secure authentication.

- Assigning websites to clients.

- Managing multiple websites per client.

- Displaying connection status.

- Detecting integration failures.

- Revoking website connections.

- Managing supported staging and production environments.



The developer may build a custom WordPress plugin where necessary.



### 12.2 Controlled Content Editing



Guardian must allow editing of approved content fields while protecting:



- Website layouts.

- Elementor templates.

- Global styling.

- Site settings.

- Unapproved widgets.

- Protected pages.

- Other unauthorized content.



Supported content should include approved:



- Headings.

- Text blocks.

- Rich text.

- Images.

- Buttons.

- Links.

- Selected Elementor fields.



The developer must document exactly which Elementor widgets and field types are supported.



Unsupported content must remain protected.



### 12.3 Drafts



Users must be able to:



- Create drafts.

- Save changes.

- Reopen drafts.

- Edit saved drafts.

- Submit drafts for approval.

- View author and modification information.



Saving a draft must not publish content.



### 12.4 Staging and Preview



Guardian must provide a safe method for previewing proposed changes before publication.



Where a staging website is available, the integration should use the approved staging environment.



The developer must document how preview functionality operates for websites without a separate staging installation.



Draft changes must not affect the public website before authorized publication.



### 12.5 Version History



Guardian must maintain immutable content versions.



Users must be able to:



- View version history.

- Identify the author of each version.

- View timestamps.

- Compare versions.

- Review changes.

- Restore eligible previous versions.



### 12.6 Approval Workflow



The platform must support:



- Submitting a specific version for review.

- Assigning authorized reviewers.

- Approving or rejecting content.

- Recording approval decisions.

- Preventing modified content from inheriting an earlier approval.

- Separating approval permissions from publishing permissions.



### 12.7 Publishing



Guardian must:



- Publish only authorized and approved content.

- Validate permissions immediately before publishing.

- Detect stale versions and conflicting changes.

- Prevent a
 overwrites.

- Record successful publishing.

- Display publishing failures.

- Preserve audit history.

- Support authorized content recovery.



### 12.8 WordPress Security



The integration must use least-privilege access.



Client portal users must not receive unrestricted WordPress administrative access.



All publishing operations must be authenticated, authorized and logged.



## 13. Website Administration



Guardian must maintain a centralized inventory of client websites.



Each website record should include:



- Client name.

- Website name.

- Primary URL.

- Primary domain.

- Additional domains.

- CMS information.

- Hosting provider.

- Hosting account reference.

- Environment information.

- SSL status.

- Maintenance responsibility.

- Website support status.

- Technical contacts.

- Administrative notes.



Guardian must support both connected WordPress websites and manually registered websites that do not use the WordPress integration.



## 14. Domain and DNS Management



Guardian must provide administrative tracking for:



- Domain registrations.

- Domain registrars.

- DNS providers.

- Nameservers.

- Domain expiration dates.

- SSL certificate status.

- SSL expiration dates.

- Renewal responsibilities.

- Domain ownership and administrative contacts.

- DNS-related support records.



The initial release must support domain and DNS recordkeeping.



Automatic domain registration, DNS modifications and registrar integrations may be developed later.



Guardian must not require clients to transfer domain ownership to Southwind.



## 15. Hosting and Infrastructure Management



Guardian must provide visibility into website hosting relationships and the infrastructure supporting Guardian itself.



### Client Website Hosting



The system must support recording:



- Hosting provider.

- Server or application reference.

- Hosting environment.

- Website association.

- Backup information.

- Maintenance status.

- SSL status.

- Hosting-related notes.

- Available monitoring data.



The architecture must accommodate future integration with Cloudways and other hosting providers.



### Guardian Application Hosting



The developer must establish and maintain a secure hosting environment for Guardian.



Required infrastructure components include:



- Frontend hosting.

- Backend services.

- Production database.

- Private file storage.

- Transactional
 delivery.

- Background jobs and scheduled processes.

- Application logs.

- Error monitoring.

- SSL/TLS.

- Backups.

- Disaster recovery procedures.

- Development and staging environments.

- Production deployment.



All infrastructure accounts must be created under Southwind's ownership and administrative control.



The developer must document the selected hosting architecture and obtain approval before activating paid services.



### Infrastructure Requirements



- Reliable deployment process.

- Secure environment variables.

- Protected API credentials.

- Access controls.

- Monitoring and alerts.

- Backup verification.

- Deployment rollback.

- Resource usage visibility.

- Cost-conscious service selection.



Guardian must be maintainable without dependence on the original developer's personal accounts.



## 16. Website Monitoring



Guardian must provide basic website availability monitoring.



Required functionality:



- Website uptime checks.

- Current availability status.

- Last successful check.

- Recent downtime history.

- Administrative alerts.

- Monitoring status.



Monitoring may use an approved third-party service or a suitable internal implementation.



Future monitoring functionality may include:



- SSL expiration alerts.

- Domain expiration alerts.

- WordPress update status.

- Plugin vulnerability monitoring.

- Hosting resource monitoring.

- Backup verification.

- Security scanning.

- Automated maintenance workflows.



Guardian must distinguish between information it directly verifies and information obtained from third-party services.



## 17. Notifications



Guardian must provide in-app notifications and transactional
 alerts.



Notification events include:



- User invitations.

- Task assignments.

- Approaching deadlines.

- Overdue tasks.

- Support ticket updates.

- Discussion replies.

- Files requiring review.

- Content approval requests.

- Approval decisions.

- Publishing results.

- Website downtime alerts.

- Important administrative events.



Users should be able to:



- View notifications.

- Mark notifications as read.

- Navigate to the relevant record.

- Manage appropriate notification preferences.



The system must avoid unnecessary duplicate notifications.



## 18. Client Onboarding and Offboarding



### Client Onboarding



Administrators must be able to:



- Create a client workspace.

- Add organization details.

- Assign staff.

- Invite client users.

- Assign contractors.

- Create projects.

- Select project templates.

- Connect websites.

- Record domain and hosting information.

- Assign service responsibilities.



### Client Offboarding



Administrators must be able to:



- Revoke user access.

- Disable integrations.

- Archive projects.

- Export authorized data.

- Preserve required audit history.

- Apply data retention and deletion policies.

- Document completion of offboarding.



Future automated onboarding through Southwind Connect must be supported by the architecture.



## 19. Search and Reporting



Guardian must support searching and filtering authorized information.



Searchable records should include:



- Clients.

- Projects.

- Tasks.

- Support tickets.

- Discussions.

- Documents.

- Websites.

- Activity history.



The platform must provide basic operational reporting, including:



- Open and completed tasks.

- Overdue work.

- Project status.

- Ticket volume and status.

- Pending approvals.

- Website monitoring events.



Advanced financial, marketing and business intelligence reporting may be developed later.



## 20. Audit Logging



Guardian must maintain audit history for significant activities.



Examples include:



- User invitations.

- Role changes.

- Access revocation.

- Security events.

- Project changes.

- Task changes.

- File access and modifications.

- Approval requests and decisions.

- Publishing events.

- Version recovery.

- Website connection changes.

- Administrative changes.



Audit events must record relevant users, timestamps, actions and affected records.



Audit logs must be protected from unauthorized modification and must not expose sensitive credentials.



## 21. Backups and Disaster Recovery



Guardian must have a documented backup and recovery strategy.



Required components:



- Automated database backups.

- File storage protection.

- Defined backup retention.

- Restricted backup access.

- Documented restoration procedures.

- Verified restore testing.

- Deployment rollback procedures.

- Application error monitoring.

- Failed-job tracking.

- Recovery documentation.



The developer must recommend appropriate recovery objectives and retention periods for Southwind's approval.



A successful restore test must be demonstrated before production acceptance.



## 22. Technical Architecture



Preferred technologies include:



- Next.js.

- React.

- TypeScript.

- PostgreSQL.

- A maintained authentication framework.

- Secure cloud object storage.

- Background-job processing.

- Well-documented APIs.

- Git-based version control.

- Automated deployment pipelines.



Equivalent technologies may be recommended when justified.



### Architecture Requirements



- Modular application structure.

- Multi-tenant database design.

- Strong authorization boundaries.

- Maintainable code.

- Secure integrations.

- Reusable components.

- API documentation.

- Environment separation.

- Automated testing.

- Scalable hosting.

- Future white-label support.

- Future subscription billing support.

- Responsive design.

- Accessible interfaces.



The developer must explain major architecture decisions and obtain approval before introducing significant dependencies.



## 23. User Interface and Experience



Guardian must provide a professional, modern interface consistent with Southwind Marketing's brand.



Requirements include:



- Responsive desktop and mobile layouts.

- Clear navigation.

- Role-specific dashboards.

- Consistent interface components.

- Accessible forms.

- Keyboard navigation.

- Clear status indicators.

- Useful validation messages.

- Confirmation of important actions.

- Efficient workflows for common tasks.



The developer must prepare interface designs for review before finalizing major modules.



Southwind will approve the design direction.



## 24. Future Development Roadmap



The following capabilities must be considered in the architecture but are not required for the initial production launch unless separately prioritized by Southwind.



### 24.1 White-Label SaaS



- Independent agency accounts.

- Agency branding.

- Custom subdomains.

- Custom domains.

- Agency-specific administration.

- Subscription plans.

- Billing integration.

- Usage limits.

- Agency-level reporting.



### 24.2 Social Media Management



-
 integration.

- Instagram integration.

- YouTube integration.

- Google Business Profile integration.

- Content calendar.

- Media uploads.

- Content approvals.

- Scheduling.

- Publishing.

- Performance reporting.



### 24.3 Reputation Management



- Review monitoring.

- Review response workflows.

- Review requests.

- Reputation reporting.



### 24.4 Southwind Connect Integration



- CRM contact synchronization.

- Client record visibility.

- Automated onboarding.

- Workflow triggers.

- Service and account information.



### 24.5 Advanced Website Management



- Cloudways API integration.

- Additional hosting-provider integrations.

- DNS-provider integrations.

- Automated SSL monitoring.

- Domain expiration alerts.

- WordPress maintenance reporting.

- Vulnerability monitoring.

- Automated website provisioning.

- Hosting administration tools.



### 24.6 Advanced Operations



- Time tracking.

- Workload management.

- Advanced recurring workflows.

- Service-level agreement tracking.

- Client satisfaction surveys.

- Resource planning.

- Advanced reporting.

- Financial integrations.



Future modules will be prioritized by Southwind leadership as the platform develops.



## 25. Development Phases



Development will proceed through defined milestones.



### Phase 1 — Architecture and Foundation



- Technical architecture.

- Database structure.

- Hosting environments.

- Authentication.

- Roles and permissions.

- Tenant isolation.

- Initial dashboard framework.

- WordPress integration proof of concept.



### Phase 2 — Core Client Operations



- Client workspaces.

- Projects.

- Tasks.

- Milestones.

- Tickets.

- Discussions.

- Documents.

- Notifications.

- Onboarding.

- Operational dashboards.



### Phase 3 — Website and Content Management



- WordPress/Elementor integration.

- Controlled editing.

- Drafts.

- Staging previews.

- Version history.

- Approval workflows.

- Publishing.

- Conflict detection.

- Recovery.

- Website inventory.

- Domain and hosting records.

- Basic website monitoring.



### Phase 4 — Testing and Production Launch



- Functional testing.

- Permission testing.

- Tenant-isolation testing.

- WordPress integration testing.

- Security review.

- Backup and restore verification.

- Production deployment.

- Documentation.

- Staff training.

- User acceptance testing.



### Phase 5 — Ongoing Development



Following launch, the developer will continue:



- Maintaining Guardian.

- Resolving defects.

- Updating dependencies.

- Monitoring infrastructure.

- Improving performance.

- Enhancing existing functionality.

- Developing approved new modules.

- Expanding integrations.

- Supporting additional Southwind development needs.



Milestone priorities and sequencing may be adjusted by Southwind based on operational needs.



## 26. Testing and Acceptance



Each major module must be demonstrated and tested before acceptance.



Required testing includes:



1. Authentication and MFA.

2. Role-based permissions.

3. Tenant isolation.

4. Contractor access restrictions.

5. Private file security.

6. Project and task workflows.

7. Ticketing and notifications.

8. WordPress connection security.

9. Elementor layout protection.

10. Draft and staging behavior.

11. Version-tied approvals.

12. Conflict detection.

13. Authorized publishing.

14. Content recovery.

15. Website monitoring.

16. Audit logging.

17. Backup restoration.

18. Responsive interface behavior.

19. Production deployment.

20. End-to-end regression testing.



Southwind must be able to independently verify that delivered functionality meets the approved requirements.



## 27. Documentation and Handover



The developer must maintain:



- Source code documentation.

- Architecture documentation.

- Database schema information.

- Deployment instructions.

- Environment configuration guidance.

- API documentation.

- WordPress plugin documentation.

- Integration records.

- Backup and recovery procedures.

- Administrative guides.

- Known limitations.

- Third-party dependency lists.

- Infrastructure and subscription records.



Documentation must be updated as the platform changes.



Another qualified developer must be able to maintain the application using the delivered documentation and repository.



## 28. Ownership and Intellectual Property



Southwind Guardian is a proprietary Southwind Marketing platform.



All custom code, designs, documentation, integrations and other deliverables developed specifically for Guardian during the engagement must be assigned to Southwind Marketing under the applicable written agreement, subject to third-party and open-source license requirements.



Southwind must maintain administrative ownership of:



- Source repositories.

- Hosting accounts.

- Databases.

- File storage.

- Domains.

- DNS accounts.

- API credentials.

- Application infrastructure.

- Monitoring services.

- Deployment systems.



Developers will receive appropriate authorized access.



The developer must not introduce undisclosed proprietary dependencies, transfer infrastructure ownership, disclose confidential information or engage unapproved subcontractors.



## 29. Ongoing Maintenance and Operational Responsibilities



As an ongoing member of Southwind's development team, the developer will be responsible for maintaining the health and reliability of Guardian.



Responsibilities include:



- Investigating production errors.

- Correcting defects.

- Maintaining security updates.

- Updating dependencies.

- Reviewing logs and alerts.

- Monitoring infrastructure health.

- Verifying backups.

- Supporting deployment and recovery.

- Improving application performance.

- Maintaining integration compatibility.

- Documenting changes.

- Assisting with user support issues.

- Planning and implementing approved enhancements.



Critical production failures and security i
 must be promptly escalated to Southwind leadership.



Production changes must follow an approved deployment process.



## 30. Communication and Development Management



The developer must:



- Provide regular progress updates.

- Maintain a current development task board.

- Record completed and outstanding work.

- Identify blockers promptly.

- Participate in scheduled reviews.

- Demonstrate completed functionality.

- Document significant technical decisions.

- Commit work regularly to Southwind's repository.

- Obtain approval for material scope or architecture changes.

- Request authorization before activating paid services.

- Coordinate with other Southwind staff and contractors as needed.



Work must remain visible and documented throughout development.



## 31. Initial Release Boundaries



The initial production launch is intended to deliver a functional client operations and WordPress management platform.



The following are not required for initial launch unless Southwind changes priorities:



- Full white-label SaaS commercialization.

- Third-party agency subscription billing.

- Complete social media publishing.

- Reputation management automation.

- Full CRM replacement.

- Native
 and SMS inbox.

- Automated DNS management.

- Domain registration services.

- Proprietary website hosting infrastructure.

- Advanced server administration.

- Native iOS and Android applications.

- Direct X/Twitter integrations.



The developer must preserve the ability to introduce these capabilities in future releases without unnecessarily rebuilding the core platform.



## 32. Developer Qualifications



The preferred developer should demonstrate experience with:



- Full-stack web application development.

- React and Next.js.

- TypeScript.

- PostgreSQL.

- Authentication and application security.

- Multi-tenant SaaS architecture.

- API development and integration.

- WordPress REST APIs.

- Elementor data structures.

- Cloud hosting and deployment.

- Database administration.

- Git workflows.

- Automated testing.

- Production troubleshooting.

- Technical documentation.



Experience developing custom WordPress plugins, agency management software, client portals, project management applications or white-label SaaS products is strongly preferred.



## 33. Application Requirements



Applicants should provide:



1. A brief professional introduction.

2. Relevant full-stack development experience.

3. Examples of applications they have personally developed.

4. Experience with multi-tenant systems.

5. Experience with WordPress and Elementor integrations.

6. Experience managing cloud hosting and production deployments.

7. Preferred technical stack.

8. Approach to security and access controls.

9. Availability and preferred working schedule.

10. Expected hourly compensation.

11. Experience working with ongoing remote teams.

12. Any major technical concerns or recommendations regarding Guardian.



Applicants should clearly identify which parts of the platform they have direct experience building.



Generic applications that do not demonstrate relevant technical experience may not be considered.



## 34. Long-Term Expectations



Southwind intends to continue developing Guardian beyond its initial launch.



The selected developer should be interested in maintaining and expanding a proprietary platform over time rather than completing a single short-term project.



Success in this role will be measured by:



- Quality and reliability of delivered functionality.

- Security and data protection.

- Consistent development progress.

- Clear communication.

- Maintainable code.

- Effective documentation.

- Responsiveness to production issues.

- Ability to work independently.

- Collaboration with Southwind leadership.

- Long-term platform stability and improvement.



Guardian is expected to become a central component of Southwind Marketing's service delivery and technology infrastructure.



The selected developer will play an important role in building and maintaining that platform.



### Required Technical Demonstration



To be considered for this position, applicants must demonstrate actual full-stack development experience. Generic portfolios, website templates, resumes, or AI-generated project proposals will not be sufficient.



Please submit:



1. **One working web application** you personally developed, preferably a SaaS platform, client portal, project management application, or similar system. Include a live demonstration link, video walkthrough, or screenshots.

2. **Your specific responsibilities** in developing that application, including frontend, backend, database, authentication, integrations, and deployment.

3. **A technical explanation** of how you implemented user authentication, permissions, and database security.

4. **One example of an API integration**, preferably WordPress, Elementor, or another third-party platform.

5. **A short video walkthrough (3–5 minutes)** demonstrating the application, its key functionality, and the code or architecture you personally worked on.

6. **Your proposed technology stack** for Southwind Guardian, along with the biggest technical challenge you anticipate and how you would approach it.



Applicants must identify which work they completed independently and which involved other developers. Do not share proprietary source code, credentials, or confidential client information.



Shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete a separate paid technical assessment.



Please include the phrase **Guardian Developer** in the first line of your application so we can confirm the full instructions were reviewed.

💼 Position Details

Position: Hiring Manager

Employment: Full-Time (40 hours/week)

Location: Fully Remote

Contract: Long-term



💡 Why Join Skinnify?

📈 Join a Hyper-Growth Brand – From 0 to 150,000+ customers in 3 years. Your hires will directly influence sales and brand growth.

🚀 Real Career Growth – Your trajectory here is whatever you make of it. One team member went from video editor to creative strategist and doubled their salary. Another started in customer support and now runs the entire customer support team. We promote from within and invest in people who want to grow.

💼 Full Flexibility – Work from anywhere, anytime. We run on trust and results, not time tracking - as long as the work gets done, your hours are yours.

🧠 Learning Budget – Courses, books, consulting calls — we cover it. Many team members book calls with founders of big ecommerce brands or managers at major companies through platforms like intro.co and mentorpass.co. 

✈️ Two Company Retreats a Year, Fully Paid – We rent a house in a new country each time, explore, and actually get to know each other. Here is a video of our last company retreat: 

⭐ Loved by the Team – Rated 5 out of 5 stars on Glassdoor (
) 



🏋️‍♀️ The Skinnify Story

Our founder Christian grew up in Frankfurt, Germany. Looking around, he noticed something striking: so many of the women in his life — his mom, his sister, his friends — wanted to get fitter, lose weight, and build muscle, but kept running into the same wall. They didn't have the time, the motivation, or the consistency to make the gym work.



The idea hit him during his own workout. He was using resistance bands and thought: what if these were built into everyday clothing? What if women could get the benefits of resistance training passively — while walking the kids to school, cooking dinner, or sitting at their desk? Fitness without the extra time or effort.



The idea was personal too. Christian was a difficult kid growing up and put his mom through a lot. She barely had time for herself, let alone the gym. He built Skinnify for women like her: busy, hardworking, often overlooked — so they could do something good for their bodies just by getting dressed.



🛍️ Our Products

What started with a single product — leggings with built-in resistance bands — has grown into a full collection of resistance-integrated clothing: leggings, sleeves, shoes, and more. We're on a mission to revolutionize how women do fitness by turning daily life into a workout.



🌟 Skinnify's Core Values

💡 Innovation – We design new, groundbreaking clothing with built-in resistance to revolutionize fitness.

🔥 Effectiveness – Our products help people burn more calories & get fitter with every step.

🌍 Accessibility – We make fitness accessible to everyone — even the busiest and least motivated.

🎉 Fun – We make exercise feel effortless and enjoyable.

✅ Quality – Our products are built to last — high-quality, durable, and reliable.

title: Client Dispute Manager (CDM) Dispute Specialist
description:
**Client Dispute Manager (CDM) Dispute Specialist — Remote Contractor**



We are a Minnesota-based credit restoration company seeking an experienced contractor to process consumer dispute files in Client Dispute Manager (CDM) and conduct a limited number of scheduled client update calls. We need someone who already knows CDM, reviews three-bureau reports carefully, communicates clearly, and maintains accurate records.



**Responsibilities**



* Import or review current reports in CDM and compare them with prior results.

* Identify potentially inaccurate or incomplete reporting and prepare individualized dispute letters following our approved procedures.

* Upload and organize supporting documents and letters, maintain clear CDM notes, and save a progress or status report in the designated client folder.

* Track dispute rounds, promptly flag missing information or report-import errors, and identify files that need management review.

* Hand completed files to the team member responsible for mailing, clearly noting anything still outstanding.

* Conduct a limited number of scheduled client update calls each week. Review the file before calling, explain the work completed and the next steps, document the conversation in CDM, and escalate questions outside our approved procedures.



We expect to build toward approximately **50 assigned client files per week** once the workflow is established. Our target is to complete each file that has all required reports, access, and documents **within one business day of assignment**. We will begin with a paid trial batch and increase volume after confirming accuracy and capacity.



**Requirements**



* Hands-on CDM experience with report imports, dispute rounds, letters, uploads, and notes.

* Understanding of Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion reports, collections, charge-offs, late payments, and dispute follow-up.

* Strong written and spoken English and a professional manner on client calls.

* Careful documentation, reliable communication, and appropriate handling of confidential client information.

* Ability to follow a documented workflow, flag exceptions promptly, and correct errors.



Experience researching collections or coordinating settlements is a plus. Settlement work is not part of the standard per-file assignment and would be discussed separately.



**Compensation:** Proposed **$10–$15 per completed client file/dispute round**, depending on experience and the agreed scope. One file means one assigned client and one specified dispute round; the number of letters may vary. Scheduled client calls will be compensated separately. We will agree on the completion checklist and payment terms before work begins. This is a contractor role.



**To apply, please answer:**



1. How long have you used CDM? Describe your workflow from report import through letters, notes, and folder organization.

2. How many client files or dispute rounds can you accurately complete in a week? What could prevent a one-business-day turnaround?

3. Describe a reporting discrepancy you caught that a template letter might have missed. Do not share client-identifying information.

4. What per-file rate do you propose for the work described above? Are you available for a paid trial batch?

5. Describe your experience giving clients phone updates. Are you available for scheduled calls during U.S. Central business hours?

6. Do you have experience researching collections or documenting settlement offers?



The paid trial will use fictional or fully de-identified material. Please do not include real client reports, account numbers, credentials, or personal information in your application.

title: Proven GoHighLevel + Automation Operator (Paid Client Builds Only)
description:
Please read this first: we only interview people who have already built GoHighLevel or automation systems for paying clients, and who can show one live in an interview. Demos, practice builds and course projects are great for learning, but they will not get you through this process.



ABOUT US

Advisor AI Solutions (AAIS) builds AI systems and automation for architecture, engineering and green building firms in Canada and the US. We also run a podcast and content program for the industry. We are a small team based in Alberta, and this role works directly with the founder.



THE ROLE

You will own a large share of client delivery: GoHighLevel builds, automations, AI tools and the reporting that goes with them. We want someone who delivers better than we could ourselves, spots a weak process, fixes it and tells us what changed. This is not an order-taker role.



MUST-HAVES

- At least 2 paid client builds in GoHighLevel and/or Make, Zapier or n8n that you shipped and that are still running (or ran for months). Built for a paying client, not for yourself.

- Willing to screen-share a live client account you built during the interview (workflows, triggers, pipelines). Hide anything private; we want to see the logic.

- Fluent spoken and written English. You will join client calls.

- Firm daily overlap with Mountain Time (Calgary): online 9 AM to 12 PM MT, Monday to Friday, every week. More overlap is welcome; less is a no.

- 25 to 40 hours per week.



NICE-TO-HAVES

- AI agents: n8n agents, voice or chat agents running for a real client.

- Outbound prospecting and list building: Sales Navigator, Apollo, Clay.

- Meta ads you set up and ran, with cost per lead.

- Content repurposing and podcast editing (Riverside or similar): clips, captions, show notes.

- Work with professional services firms (architecture, engineering, construction).



PAY AND CONTRACT

- Monthly pay: USD 800 to 1,200 per month, based on proven work. Please quote a monthly rate in USD.

- Weekly hour cap agreed up front.

- Tell us how many active clients you have now and how many hours a week each takes. We check this against your profile, so please be accurate. Other clients are fine; surprises are not.



HOW TO APPLY

Apply here by following these steps. We read every application that follows them and skip the rest.

1. Start your application with the word SHIPPED.

2. Link or describe 2 paid client builds. For each: the client type, what you built, the tools, and the result it drove (for example leads, booked calls, hours saved).

3. State your exact daily overlap window in Mountain Time.

4. State your monthly rate in USD.

5. State your current active clients and the hours you give each.

6. Answer the screening questions in your own words. Short and specific beats long and polished. We can tell when answers are written by AI or read from a script.



Include a Loom showing a live client GoHighLevel account you built (paid client work only).



HIRING PROCESS

1. Short screen (15 minutes): rate, hours, overlap, client load.

2. Live screen-share interview (30 minutes): you walk us through a live client build and we ask how it works and what broke.

3. Paid trial task (2 to 3 hours, paid pro rata at your agreed monthly rate, no client data).

4. Decision within a week of the trial.



Target start: early November 2026.



SCREENING QUESTIONS (answer these in your application)

1. Describe 2 paid client builds in GoHighLevel, Make, Zapier or n8n that are live today or ran for months. For each: client type, what you built, the contract size in USD, and one measurable result (for example leads, booked calls, hours saved). If you have fewer than 2, say so.

2. Pick one of those builds. What broke after it went live, how did you find out, and exactly what did you change in the workflow to fix it?

3. In the interview you will screen-share a live client account you built. Which account will you show (client type only), and what will we see in it: which workflows, triggers, pipelines or integrations?

4. What are your exact working hours, Monday to Friday, in your time zone and in Mountain Time? Confirm you can be online 9 AM to 12 PM MT every weekday.

5. What is your monthly rate in USD, how many hours a week can you give us, and how many active clients do you have right now (with hours per week for each)?

This is not a basic assistant role. We are not looking for someone who waits for instructions, disappears during work hours, or escalates every problem. We hold ourselves to a very high standard, and we will hold you to that same standard.



SCHEDULE

WHAT YOU WILL OWN

title: AI Marketing, Systems & Automation VA – Full-Time
description:
AI Marketing, Systems & Automation VA – Full-Time



$4 USD/hour | 40 hours per week | Long-term role with opportunity to grow



We are a growing digital marketing agency managing 15+ clients and are looking for a full-time AI Marketing, Systems & Automation VA to join our team.



This is not a traditional Social Media Manager or Ads Manager role.



We are looking for someone who is highly interested in AI, automation, systems and new technology and can help us make our agency faster, smarter, more organised and more efficient.



You should naturally think:



“How can AI or automation make this better, faster or easier?”



MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES



1. AI & AUTOMATION



We want to integrate AI throughout our agency.



You will use tools such as ChatGPT, Claude and other emerging AI platforms to:



• Create and improve content  

• Assist with website creation  

• Build repeatable AI workflows  

• Automate repetitive tasks  

• Research and test new AI tools  

• Improve existing processes  

• Find ways to deliver better services to our clients  

• Keep up with developments in AI and digital marketing  



Alos manage and monitor ad accounts 



We don't want to continue doing something manually simply because that's how it has always been done.



2. CONTENT & VIDEO



You will help manage content production across 15+ client accounts.



This will include:



• Using AI to create social media plans, ideas and captions  

• Creating and adapting Canva graphics  

• Short-form video editing  

• Creating Reels and advertising creatives  

• Repurposing existing content  

• Scheduling content  

• Quality checking content before it is sent to clients  

• Making sure client content is completed on time  

• Developing systems that allow us to batch-create content efficiently  



We want to move towards creating 2–3 months of client content at a time using repeatable systems, templates and AI.



AI should be heavily used to speed up production, but quality control is extremely important. Content should not look or sound obviously AI-generated.



3. SYSTEMS & TEAM ORGANISATION



A major part of this role will be helping us improve how the agency operates internally.



We currently use ClickUp and want to build a much more automated system.



You will help:



• Build and maintain our ClickUp system  

• Automate recurring client tasks  

• Track deadlines and deliverables  

• Keep team members on track  

• Make sure tasks aren't missed  

• Set up automated reminders and follow-ups  

• Improve client onboarding  

• Build workflows for content, websites, leads and other services  

• Identify bottlenecks  

• Keep systems organised and up to date  



The goal is to create an agency where very little relies on someone manually remembering what needs to happen next.



4. CLIENT SERVICE & INNOVATION



We want our clients to feel they are receiving a modern, technology-driven marketing service.



You will be encouraged to research and test new tools, AI platforms and automations that could improve what we offer.



We want someone who proactively brings ideas to us rather than waiting to be told about every new tool or process.



WHAT ABOUT ADS?



Advertising is not the main focus of this role, but you should have a good understanding of Meta Ads and ideally Google Ads.



You may occasionally help with:



• Checking campaigns  

• Creating ad copy and creatives  

• Reviewing basic performance  

• Creating reports  

• Making straightforward campaign changes  





WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



You should be:



• Very comfortable using AI  

• Experienced with ChatGPT and/or Claude  

• Highly interested in automation  

• Comfortable with ClickUp or similar systems  

• Good at creating social media content  

• Able to edit short-form videos  

• Comfortable with Canva  

• Familiar with Meta Ads  

• Technically confident  

• Extremely organised  

• Able to keep yourself and other team members on track  

• A fast learner  

• Good at researching solutions independently  

• Proactive rather than waiting for instructions  

• Comfortable learning new software  

• Able to communicate clearly in English  



We are not looking for someone who needs step-by-step instructions for every task.



We want someone who can be given a problem or outcome, research it, use AI to help solve it and implement a solution.



TOOLS WE USE



Experience with any of the following is useful:



ChatGPT | Claude | ClickUp | GoHighLevel | Make | Zapier | Canva | CapCut | Meta Ads | Google Ads | WordPress | Wix | Webflow

title: Job Description: Amazon Virtual Assistant (Canada & USA)

title: Senior Full-Stack Developer / Technical Architect
description:

About the Project



We are building DAASS Real Estate OS, a powerful, proprietary software platform that will serve as the central operating system for our real estate investing academy students.



We already have a collection of useful real estate tools built in Lovable. Now, we want to take the next step: build a much stronger, fully integrated, production-grade platform from the ground up.



We are not looking for someone to simply add features to our existing Lovable application. We need an experienced engineer who can use our existing tools as references, preserve valuable functionality, and architect a superior platform designed for long-term growth.



We are open to the best technology stack for the job. AI-assisted development is encouraged, but we need a serious developer who understands the code, architecture, and engineering decisions behind the product.



What We're Building



The platform will connect three major areas of real estate investing:



Acquire: Market research, deal sourcing, off-market leads, CRM, property analysis, AI comps and ARV, rehab estimating, offers, and closing.

- Operate: Property management, tenants, rent tracking, maintenance, bookkeeping, compliance, and portfolio reporting.

- Multifamily: Commercial deal sourcing, underwriting, financial modeling, capital raise tracking, and asset management.



All modules must work together through a shared foundation of property records, CRM, contacts, documents, tasks, financial calculations, and integrations.



For example, when a student acquires a property, its data, financing, rehab plan, photos, and documents should flow directly into the operating system. Information should be entered once and reused throughout the platform.



Each student must have a secure, individual workspace with their own properties, deals, contacts, documents, and financial data.



Our goal is one cohesive operating system, not a collection of disconnected tools.



 What We're Looking For



We need a developer who can architect, build, and maintain a sophisticated SaaS application, with strong experience in:



- Full-stack software development and system architecture.

- Database design, APIs, and interconnected application modules.

- Multi-tenant applications, authentication, and data security.

- Third-party integrations and AI-powered features.

- Reliable financial calculations and data-intensive workflows.

- Modern UI/UX and consistent design systems.

- Testing, debugging, deployment, and ongoing maintenance.



Experience with React, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Supabase, or comparable technologies is valuable. Experience building CRMs, SaaS platforms, financial applications, or real estate software is a major plus.



We embrace modern AI coding tools and agents. However, we need an engineer who can use AI to build faster without sacrificing code quality, security, or reliability. This is not a role for someone who simply generates screens in Lovable.



The Ideal Candidate



You are a systems thinker who understands how an entire product fits together. You write maintainable code, anticipate technical challenges, make sound architectural decisions, and communicate clearly.



You can work independently, recommend better approaches when necessary, and take ownership of the product's long-term technical quality.

title: Operations Manager: Short-Term Rentals (US Graveyard Shift)
description:
OPERATIONS MANAGER: SHORT-TERM RENTALS (US GRAVEYARD SHIFT)



Please read this whole post before applying. There are instructions at the bottom, and how you follow them is the first thing we look at.



ABOUT US



We run short-term rental and vacation rental hosting for owners across the US, fully hands-off. An owner hands us a home. We furnish it, wire it, stock it, style it, photograph it, register it with the city, connect it to Airbnb and Vrbo and the other booking channels, and open it to guests. Then somebody runs every stay, every turnover, every vendor call and every 3:00 AM alarm, for as long as that owner stays with us. That second part is this seat.



Nine homes are earning revenue today, eleven are live with us across four US markets, and fourteen hosting agreements are signed. Every owner we have came from a referral. Nobody found us in a search, which means our reputation is not a marketing asset, it is the entire pipeline. A guest who walks into a home that is not ready costs us a review, and a review costs us the next owner. Most days in this seat are a dispatch board, a photo set, a vendor who has not called back, a shift log, a hiring pipeline and one decision that has to be made now on two-thirds of the information. Operations, vendor management, scheduling, escalation, owner communication and hospitality customer service, on US hours.



We automate everything software can do. What software cannot do is notice that a cleaner has fired thirty-two not-started alerts in twenty-six days and nobody has counted them, or notice that a pool vendor billed us every month all summer and two of those months reached no invoice at all.



Our written plan is 150 homes by the end of 2027. Eleven is where we are. The gap between those two numbers is not a software problem and it is not a sales problem. It is whether the operation holds when it is four times the size, which is exactly why we are hiring a person to run it.



WHAT THIS ROLE REALLY IS



We have five people covering guest operations twenty-four hours a day, and none of them has a manager. Five separate one-to-one relationships with our founder. Five windows that tile the week perfectly and overlap nowhere. Nobody runs the handoffs, nobody scores the turns, nobody holds a vendor to a second chance, and every problem that falls between two shifts lands on one phone. That is the seat.



Two lanes, one person. Every case below is real. The dollar amounts are changed. The counts, the dates and the shapes are not.



LANE ONE, THE OPERATION ON THE GROUND.



- Thirty-two not-started cleaning alerts fired in twenty-six days across four cleaners. One cleaner fired three no-show alerts in a single week on a single door. Four of the thirty-two landed on live same-day flips with a 4:00 PM arrival. A chronic no-show survived months, because nothing counted them.

- A house that sleeps twelve takes about sixteen labor hours to turn as our checklist is written, thirteen once a crew knows it. On a 10:00 AM out and a 4:00 PM in, four trained people finish at 2:53 PM, three at 3:56 PM, and two after 6:00 PM. Somebody has to make that call on Thursday. Nobody does, so we find out on Saturday.

- A damage claim after a party asked for $584.10 and collected $77.20. Soaked mattress, ruined linens, broken skimmer cover, all real. The turnover photos that would have proved the before-state lived in a text thread and never reached the evidence folder. We lost that on filing, not on the facts.

- A recurring pool vendor bills $370 a month at one home. June reached an owner invoice. July and August reached nothing, and no payment record exists for either, so it is not even clear the vendor got paid. About $740 sat invisible for two months, because nothing watches a recurring vendor against what we actually billed.

- A door went live with instant booking on and no named first-call vendor in its file for a lockout, a leak, a power cut or a dead AC. The water main shutoff is written down nowhere. Neither is the gas shutoff, and neither is the breaker panel. The printed house rules still carry a placeholder where the 24-hour local contact's name belongs. Eleven weeks earlier, at 3:39 AM, a guest at another home reported a gas alarm and was told to get outside and call 911, because there was nobody local to send.

- A home launched mid-renovation and sits at 4.60. The first guests found the hot water running out in a house that sleeps ten, half the kitchen outlets dead, a second fridge taped shut and never plugged in, a dead hot tub, an empty propane tank, and glass in the driveway. Then somebody edited the permanent guest guide to tell future guests to stagger their showers. A launch defect became a house rule. One guest's actual words: "I just wish you had been honest upfront."



LANE TWO, THE TEAM, THE RECORD AND THE ESCALATIONS.



- Our five contractors cover 168 of 168 hours a week with exactly one person on every hour and zero overlap anywhere. That is a tiling, not depth. One sick night is a fully uncovered block. Twenty-six handoffs a week, and every one of them is cold, so a single skipped log post drops a live guest thread at a shift boundary.

- Guest-money authority was granted to the team in July, written down, and exercised almost never. Sixty-seven of seventy-two shift logs read "Money today: NONE," because two pinned channel rules still routed every purchase and every comp through our founder "until he says otherwise," and he never said otherwise. His own message volume went 47, then 71, then 97, then 192, then 201 a week as the team grew.

- Half our automation was silently dead for five weeks and nobody knew. Guest reply drafting off since late July, the daily brief dead since the 22nd, inbox triage dead since the 9th, one job failed 520 times in a row. Nothing alerted, because the health check measured whether a log file was fresh rather than whether the job worked, and a crashing job writes a fresh log.

- A sweep across nine homes found exactly one ready to run hands-off. One door had thirty-one gaps against fourteen filled. Seventy-two punch-list items are still open and the task board reads 484 open with 45 never triaged.

- Four known wrong facts have sat live on listings for months: house rules claiming a noise monitor that is not installed, a check-in message describing a hot tub that does not exist, a photo of a removed fireplace, a wifi password that does not match the house. Every one is handled by a human overriding it by hand, on every shift, forever.

- Nobody on our technician roster has a W-9 on file. No written services agreement with a cleaning company exists anywhere in the company. Every term we care about lives in somebody's memory of a phone call.

- An owner asked a question about her own statement and waited five days, with a follow-up in between. Two more owners waited three and five days on theirs. Nobody owned the reply.



The honest description of this role: you are building an operations team from nothing while the operation is already running, and the running one is louder.



THE PART TO READ TWICE. On day one, nobody reports to you. There is no ops team to take over. There are five contractors who each talk to our founder separately, a vendor list where half the numbers have never been dialed, and a written standard that is good and is not enforced. The first six months is hiring, writing, wiring and proving. The managing comes after you have built something to manage. If what you want is to walk into a functioning department and run it well, this is the wrong post, and we would rather say so here than find out together in month three.

This is not task-list work. Nobody will send you a list each morning telling you which turnover to check or which vendor to chase. You run a weekly scoreboard, a dispatch board and a hiring pipeline you built yourself, so you already know.



On our tools, so the form does not have to ask you about them. WHAT YOU WILL OWN



THE TURNOVER MACHINE. Every checkout becomes a turn, the turn is the highest-volume event in this business, and it is yours end to end.

- The same-day flip call. You size the crew against the house days ahead, and you enforce the checkpoint ninety minutes before check-in where a crew that will not finish calls us instead of pushing through and hoping.

- The CLEAR and HOLD gate. No turn reads done without the lock test performed with the arriving guest's own code, and every after-photo uploaded, including the two grounds shots. A HOLD is a phone call, never a checkbox, and you are the human who answers it.

- The turn scorecard nobody runs today: photos, on-time, inspection, guest feedback, rolling thirty-day, per cleaner.

- Below the line for two weeks is a retraining conversation. Below the floor is reassignment. You have both conversations.

- The monthly device round and the linen par. Three devices in every home fail silently and all three already have. A six-bedroom house generates twelve to fifteen loads a turn against about four loads of washer capacity in the window, so the swap model is physics, not preference.
